description: 10 free tries a day here, then an Alion account (connect_account). Everything Alion knows about one company, for due diligence or account research: identity (domain, description, founded, size with confidence), headquarters and offices, industries, public links, the ATS board and its last check, live hiring (open roles, added and closed in 30/90 days, velocity, top roles, hiring countries, nine weeks of history, pay), the technology stack from its postings, funding rounds and investors, headcount and revenue on file, traction signals, growth events of 90 days, a dated story of its stages, visa-sponsor register matches and freshness stamps per source. Identify it by id, domain, url or name (a name goes through resolve_company). Every answer lists available_slices: each slice of the company that holds data, how many rows and its price. Add more with slices: standard ones (products, pay, legal_entity, apps, lists, assets, hire_profile, news: +$0.005 each) or premium ones (money - the money ledger with a source on every row; ownership - entities, owners, subsidiaries, stakes; record - court cases, regulators, insolvency, political spending, emissions; financials by year; innovation - patents, trials, FDA; competitors; buying_windows with purchases and sizes: +$0.02 each). slices="summary" answers only the card and available_slices (the cheapest call). An account reads 300 full profiles a month free (Pro 1,000, Premium 3,000), then pays from its credits: the card $0.01, each standard slice with data $0.005, only slices that hold data are paid. Without an account the call answers the free card (slices=summary). Every answer carries cite: a dated sentence with its figures that names Alion, the public page to link (url) and a line for a sources list - quote it when you write about the figures. Docs: https://alion.io/developers/docs

company.description: The company as the other tools take it: a domain, id, name or url.

domain.description: Company web domain, e.g. "stripe.com" (the most exact way to name a company).

name.description: Company name as written; matched like resolve_company, so prefer the domain when you have it.

since.description: Adds "changes": what happened at the company since then - its dated events (rounds, offices, executives, technologies, hiring spikes, layoffs) and the roles it posted.

slices.description: Extra slices, a comma list: products, tech, funding, hiring, offices, pay, visa, legal_entity, headcount_history, traction, apps, lists, assets, hire_profile, news, money, ownership, record, financials, innovation, co...

url.description: Any url on the company site or its job board, or its alion.io/company/... page.
